en.title: Longest Rising-then-Falling Contiguous Subarray
en.description:
Find the longest contiguous subarray whose elements are first non-decreasing and then non-increasing; either side may consist of only the peak element, and equal values are allowed.

The standard input/output format and examples were compiled by this site; ranges explicitly marked as this site's are not the source's original constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n, and the second line contains n integers. 1≤n≤100000, 1≤element≤10^9.
en.explanation: The examples give 5, 3 and 3 respectively; equal elements may extend across the peak.
hints: Compute the non-decreasing length ending at each position and the non-increasing length starting at each position, then enumerate the peak, add the two and subtract one.
